title: 3Sum
contract: Return distinct sorted triples summing to zero. Return triples in lexicographic textual order for deterministic comparison.
brute: Set<String> out=new TreeSet<>();for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++)for(int j=i+1;j<a.length;j++)for(int k=j+1;k<a.length;k++){emit("Test three indices","indices",new int[]{i,j,k});if((long)a[i]+a[j]+a[k]==0){int[] t={a[i],a[j],a[k]};Arrays.sort(t);out.add(Arrays.toString(t));}}return new ArrayList<>(out);
optimal: Arrays.sort(a);Set<String> out=new TreeSet<>();for(int i=0;i<a.length-2;i++){if(i>0&&a[i]==a[i-1])continue;int l=i+1,r=a.length-1;while(l<r){long sum=(long)a[i]+a[l]+a[r];emit("Fix one value and shrink a sorted pair range","indices",new int[]{i,l,r},"sum",sum);if(sum<0)l++;else if(sum>0)r--;else{out.add(Arrays.toString(new int[]{a[i],a[l],a[r]}));int left=a[l],right=a[r];while(l<r&&a[l]==left)l++;while(l<r&&a[r]==right)r--;}}}return new ArrayList<>(out);
reasoning: Enumerate index triples and deduplicate their sorted value representations.
Sort once, fix the first value, then move the pair pointers according to whether the sum is too small or too large.
Skip repeated fixed values and repeated matched endpoints. Widen before addition. Sorting textual answers adds output-ordering cost beyond the numeric search.
complexity: O(n² + z log z), O(z) output plus sort workspace
